findings.claim: The two newly re-exported type names (`inferSubscriptionInput`, `inferSubscriptionOutput`) must actually be exported from the source module of this `export { ... } from` statement, otherwise this file fails to compile.
findings.rationale: The hunk only shows the export list, not the module it re-exports from (typically `../../unstable-core-do-not-import`). If these helper types were added under different names (e.g. `inferSubscriptionOutput` defined only locally, or exported as part of a namespace) the re-export is a TS2459/TS2305 error. Medium confidence — worth verifying the core module exports both names; also verify neither name is already re-exported elsewhere in this index file, which would cause a duplicate-export conflict.

findings.claim: Adding these to the public entrypoint permanently widens the public API surface; if the underlying types are experimental/unstable they should not be exported from the stable `@trpc/server` index.
findings.rationale: This file is the package's public entrypoint, so anything exported here becomes a semver-stable contract. Subscription-related inference helpers are often still in flux; exporting them here means future renames/signature changes are breaking. Low-to-medium confidence since I cannot see the definitions, but the placement in the stable index (rather than an `unstable-`/`experimental` entrypoint) is worth a second look.
